unit.title: Investigating 3D Shapes and Nets
unit.blurb: Faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids, and nets that fold to make cubes, cuboids, prisms and pyramids.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Identify, describe and sort 3D shapes by their faces, edges and vertices.

O2.t: Identify and sketch nets of cubes, cuboids, prisms and pyramids.

p: A **prism** has the same shape at both ends, joined by rectangles. A **pyramid** has a base and triangular faces meeting at a point (the apex).
A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices.
Some edges and vertices are at the back. Dashed lines show them.

p: A **net** is a flat shape that folds up into a 3D shape. A cube has 11 different nets, each of 6 squares.
A net of a square-based pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles. A net of a triangular prism has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.
If two squares fold onto the same place, it is not a net of a cube.
